title: Module Overview: From Degree Criterion to Galois Criterion
content:
The file imports Mathlib (for p-groups, Galois groups, field extensions, polynomials) plus four project-local files: `InverseGalois` (S₃ as Galois group of x³-2), `InverseGaloisD4` (D₄ as Galois group of x⁴-2), `NthRootIrrationalOQ01` (irreducibility of x^n-a), and `AngleTrisectionCos20Gal` (Galois group of the trisection polynomial). The module docstring explains the upgrade from OQ-01's necessary condition (degree divides 2^n) to OQ-02's exact biconditional (constructibility ↔ 2-group Galois). This is a fundamental shift: degree is a numerical shadow of the richer group-theoretic structure.

**Why the upgrade matters:** The degree criterion alone cannot distinguish √2 (constructible, degree 2) from ∛2 (non-constructible, degree 3). But it also fails more subtly: there exist algebraic numbers whose degree IS a power of 2 but which are NOT constructible — because the Galois group, though of 2-power order, may not embed into the right intermediate field structure. The 2-group Galois criterion captures the exact obstruction.
mathContext: The upgrade: OQ-01 says $\alpha$ constructible $\Rightarrow [\mathbb{Q}(\alpha):\mathbb{Q}] \mid 2^n$ (necessary). OQ-02 says $\alpha$ constructible $\iff \text{Gal}(\text{minpoly}(\mathbb{Q},\alpha))$ is a 2-group (necessary AND sufficient).

title: 2-Groups: Order-Power-of-Two Characterization
content: Three theorems establishing the equivalence between `IsPGroup 2 G` and having order a power of 2: `isPGroup_iff_card_pow_two` (iff direction from `IsPGroup.iff_card`), `isPGroup_of_card_pow_two` (2-power order implies 2-group via `IsPGroup.of_card`), and `isPGroup_card_is_pow_two` (the converse). These basic facts are the gateway to the Galois-group-based constructibility criterion — the key predicate is whether the Galois group has order 2ⁿ.
mathContext: A group $G$ is a **$p$-group** if every element has order a power of $p$. For finite groups, $G$ is a $p$-group $\iff$ $|G| = p^n$ for some $n \geq 0$. For $p = 2$: 2-groups include $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$, $D_4$, $Q_8$. Non-2-groups include $S_3$ (order 6), $\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}$ (order 3). In Mathlib, `IsPGroup p G` is defined element-wise; the order characterization `IsPGroup.iff_card` requires `[Fintype G]`. The `Nat.card` form (used in `IsPGroup.iff_card`) differs from `Fintype.card` but they agree for finite types via `Nat.card_eq_fintype_card`.

title: IsConstructibleFromQ: Tower Condition for Constructibility
content: `IsConstructibleFromQ α` requires α to lie in an intermediate field K of ℝ/ℚ that is (1) finite-dimensional over ℚ and (2) has degree [K:ℚ] = 2ⁿ for some n. This captures the tower of degree-2 field extensions generated by compass-and-straightedge: each step adds a square root (degree-2 extension), because the only 'new' operation compass and straightedge provide beyond field operations is intersecting a circle with a line/circle, which introduces at most a square root via the quadratic formula. The definition uses `IntermediateField ℚ ℝ` to work inside ℝ directly, rather than an abstract field extension, and `Module.finrank ℚ K` (not the deprecated `finrank` or `IsFiniteDimensional`) for the degree.
mathContext: Formally: $\alpha$ is constructible iff $\exists K$ with $\mathbb{Q} \subseteq K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, $[K:\mathbb{Q}] = 2^n$, and $\alpha \in K$. This is equivalent to: $\alpha$ reachable from $\mathbb{Q}$ by $(+, -, \times, \div, \sqrt{\cdot})$ with real outputs. Key: $[K:\mathbb{Q}] = 2^n$ rules out extensions of degree $3, 5, 6, 7, \ldots$ — ∛2 requires degree 3, cos(20°) requires degree 3, neither fits in a degree-$2^n$ extension.

title: Wantzel-Galois Theorem: Constructibility ↔ 2-Group Galois
content:
`wantzel_galois_characterization` is the main axiom: `IsConstructibleFromQ α ↔ IsPGroup 2 (minpoly ℚ α).Gal`. The docstring explains both proof directions: (→) α in a degree-2 tower gives a splitting field K with [K:ℚ] = 2^m, so Gal(K/ℚ) is a 2-group, and Gal(minpoly) embeds as a subgroup. (←) A 2-group Galois group has a composition series with ℤ/2ℤ quotients — by the Galois correspondence, this gives a degree-2 extension tower, so α is constructible. Axiomatized because the full proof needs the Galois correspondence.

**Hierarchy of expressibility:** Constructibility (2-group Galois) is strictly more restrictive than solvability by radicals (solvable Galois group, per Abel-Ruffini). Every 2-group is solvable (composition factors are ℤ/2ℤ, which is abelian), but not every solvable group is a 2-group. Example: Gal(x⁵-2/ℚ) ≅ F₂₀ (Frobenius group of order 20 = 4·5) is solvable (with derived series F₂₀ ▷ ℤ/5ℤ ▷ {e}), so ⁵√2 is solvable by radicals, but F₂₀ is not a 2-group, so ⁵√2 is NOT constructible.

**Fermat prime connection:** For the celebrated regular polygon problem: cos(2π/p) is constructible iff Gal(ℚ(ζₚ)/ℚ) ≅ ℤ/(p-1)ℤ is a 2-group, i.e., p-1 = 2ⁿ, i.e., p is a Fermat prime. Only 5 Fermat primes are known (3, 5, 17, 257, 65537), and it remains open whether there are finitely or infinitely many.
mathContext: **Wantzel-Galois**: $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$ is constructible $\iff$ $\text{Gal}(\text{minpoly}(\mathbb{Q}, \alpha)/\mathbb{Q})$ is a 2-group. Proof sketch ($\Leftarrow$): 2-groups are solvable; by Jordan-Hölder, composition factors are $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$; by Galois correspondence, each factor corresponds to a degree-2 extension — exactly what compass-and-straightedge produces. The `.Gal` in `(minpoly ℚ α).Gal` is `Polynomial.Gal`: the Galois group of the splitting field of a polynomial over the base field.

title: Non-Constructibility: Coprimality Proves Order 6 Is Not a 2-Power
content: The private lemma `not_pow_two_of_eq_six` proves `6 ≠ 2^n` by contradiction: if `6 = 2^n`, then `Coprime 3 (2^n)` (since gcd(3,2)=1 implies gcd(3,2^n)=1 via `Nat.Coprime.pow_right`), but `3 ∣ 2^n` (since 3 ∣ 6 = 2^n). A number coprime to n cannot divide n. This drives both non-constructibility proofs: for `x_cube_sub_2_gal_not_2group` and `cos20_gal_not_2group`, the axioms give `|Gal| = 6`, then `IsPGroup.iff_card.mp` extracts `Nat.card = 2^n`, and `not_pow_two_of_eq_six` gives the contradiction.
mathContext: Coprimality argument: $3 \nmid 2^n$ for any $n$ because $\gcd(3, 2) = 1 \Rightarrow \gcd(3, 2^n) = 1$ (coprimality preserved under powers), so 3 cannot divide $2^n$. But $3 \mid 6$, hence $6 \neq 2^n$. In Lean 4: `Nat.Coprime.pow_right n (by norm_num : Nat.Coprime 3 2)` gives `Coprime 3 (2^n)`, then `Nat.dvd_gcd (dvd_refl 3) h3dvd` constructs the contradiction. The same lemma serves both: $\text{Gal}(x^3-2/\mathbb{Q}) \cong S_3$ (order 6) and $\text{Gal}(8x^3-6x-1/\mathbb{Q}) \cong S_3$ (order 6, the triple-angle formula polynomial for cos(20°)).

title: Constructible Examples: √2 (ℤ/2ℤ, order 2) and 2^(1/4) (D₄, order 8)
content:
`x_sq_sub_2_gal_is_2group` proves Gal(x²-2/ℚ) is a 2-group via `IsPGroup.of_card` with `Nat.card = 2^1`, using `simp [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, x_sq_sub_2_gal_order]` to convert the `Fintype.card = 2` axiom. Similarly, `x_4th_sub_2_gal_is_2group` proves order 8 = 2³. Both use the same `IsPGroup.of_card` pattern with explicit `show Nat.card ... = 2^_` goals. Combined with `wantzel_galois_characterization`, these confirm √2 and 2^(1/4) are constructible.

Geometrically: √2 is constructible because it is the diagonal of a unit square (one compass-straightedge step from the unit length). 2^(1/4) = √(√2) requires two successive square root extractions, each corresponding to a degree-2 field extension — exactly matching the D₄ Galois group's composition series with three ℤ/2ℤ quotients.
mathContext: - $\text{Gal}(x^2 - 2/\mathbb{Q}) \cong \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ (order $2 = 2^1$): only automorphism is $\sqrt{2} \mapsto -\sqrt{2}$. - $\text{Gal}(x^4 - 2/\mathbb{Q}) \cong D_4$ (dihedral group, order $8 = 2^3$): the four roots are $\zeta^k \sqrt[4]{2}$ for $\zeta = i$ and the Galois group acts by permuting them. Both groups are 2-groups ($|G| = 2^1$ and $|G| = 2^3$). The pattern `IsPGroup.of_card (show Nat.card ... = 2^k from by simp ...)` is the idiomatic Lean 4 way to establish 2-group membership from a cardinality axiom.

title: OQ-02 Strictly Strengthens OQ-01: Galois Criterion Implies Degree Criterion
content: `constructible_implies_degree_dvd_pow2` chains two steps: constructibility → (Galois 2-group via `wantzel_galois_characterization`) → (degree ∣ 2^n via `galois_2group_implies_degree_pow2`). This shows OQ-02 implies OQ-01 but not vice versa. The degree criterion is necessary but not sufficient for constructibility; the Galois criterion is the exact characterization. The axiom `galois_2group_implies_degree_pow2` captures the fact that `natDegree(minpoly) ∣ |Gal|` and 2-groups have 2-power order.
mathContext: The logical chain: Constructible $\Rightarrow$ Gal is 2-group $\Rightarrow$ deg $\mid 2^n$. Reverse failures: degree = $2^k$ does NOT imply Gal is a 2-group (some degree-$2^k$ polynomials have non-2-group Galois groups via composita). The key fact used is that `natDegree(p) ∣ |Gal(p)|` (Galois group order is divisible by the degree for irreducible polynomials), so $|\text{Gal}| = 2^m \Rightarrow \text{deg} \mid 2^m$.

title: Contrapositive Non-Constructibility: Two Routes
content: Part VII provides two contrapositive forms. `not_constructible_of_not_2group`: rewrites along `wantzel_galois_characterization` and applies `¬ IsPGroup 2 (minpoly ℚ α).Gal`. `not_constructible_of_degree`: a one-liner `fun hc => h _ (constructible_implies_degree_dvd_pow2 α hα hc)` — assumes constructibility, derives degree divisibility, applies the hypothesis that no n works. The Galois route requires knowing the Galois group structure; the degree route is weaker but easier when only the degree is known.
mathContext:
Two contrapositive forms: 1. **Galois route**: $
eg(	ext{Gal is 2-group}) \Rightarrow 
eg\alpha$ constructible. Direct from the iff. 2. **Degree route**: $( orall n, 	ext{deg} 
mid 2^n) \Rightarrow 
eg\alpha$ constructible. Follows from constructible $\Rightarrow$ deg $\mid 2^n$. Example uses: cos(20°) via Galois route (S₃, order 6); an odd-degree irreducible polynomial via degree route (degree 3 does not divide any $2^n$ since $2 
mid 3$).

title: Summary: 22 Declarations, 1 Axiom
content:
The file contains 15 public theorems, 2 private lemmas, 4 private theorems, 1 definition (`IsConstructibleFromQ`), and 1 axiom (`wantzel_galois_characterization`). The Galois group orders for x³-2 and cos(20°)'s minimal polynomial are proved (not axiomatized) — they reference results in companion files InverseGalois.lean and AngleTrisectionCos20Gal.lean.

The only axiom remaining is `wantzel_galois_characterization` (the biconditional requiring the full Galois correspondence). All other results are either proved from Mathlib lemmas or derived from first principles.

**Verification methodology:** The six `#check` commands at the end test both proved theorems and imported results: `isPGroup_iff_card_pow_two` (basic 2-group fact), `x_cube_sub_2_gal_not_2group` (∛2 non-constructible), `cos20_gal_not_2group` (trisection impossible), `x_sq_sub_2_gal_is_2group` (√2 constructible), `x_4th_sub_2_gal_is_2group` (2^(1/4) constructible), and `constructible_implies_degree_dvd_pow2` (OQ-02 implies OQ-01).
mathContext: 22 total declarations: 15 public theorems + 6 private lemmas/theorems + 1 definition + 1 axiom. The sole axiom `wantzel_galois_characterization` is the only gap: it requires the Galois correspondence $\text{Gal}(K/\mathbb{Q})$ subgroups $\leftrightarrow$ intermediate fields, which Mathlib provides but the full proof chain is complex.
